fixture_purpose: Demonstrates that malformed SHA-256 values are rejected before any DB write. Two-layer defense: MCP input validation then SQLite CHECK constraints.

layer_1_mcp_validation.rule: length must equal 64 and every character must be in [0-9a-f]. Returns false for short, long, uppercase, or non-hex inputs. MCP handler maps false to -32023 (malformed_lead_decision_sha256 or malformed_continuation_instruction_sha256) before any DB interaction.

layer_2_sqlite_check.rule: SHA-256 columns use: CHECK (length(c) = 64 AND c NOT GLOB '*[^0-9a-f]*'). Nullable columns add: c IS NULL OR (...). SQLite rejects any INSERT/UPDATE where a non-null SHA-256 column fails this predicate.

evidence.hold_predicate_prevented: No malformed hash can enter the system. MCP validation rejects before DB write; SQLite CHECK provides defense-in-depth for any future code path that bypasses the MCP layer.
